answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network applies topological cut verifications across the trust graph: if an attacker floods an ocean of fake nodes, multi-agent auditing traps fraudulent clusters within a sparse cut. Auditing agents stake tokens, slashing collateral upon false validation. Because certifying isolated cut boundaries requires superlinear collateral growth, masking malicious subgraphs behind a sable veil or violet boundary incurs superlinear attacker cost.
